plates.side_label: JUNE 1845 TRAIN HORN (G4 = 392 HZ): APPROACH 414 HZ (+1 SEMITONE) → RECEDE 372 HZ (−1 SEMITONE)
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked musical-pitch and wavelength chart from Buys Ballot's June 1845 Utrecht–Maarssen train experiments shows a sustained G4 horn note (~392 Hz): approaching at ~18 m/s (~40 mph) shifts pitch up to ~414 Hz (~G#4, +1 semitone), then drops on passing to ~372 Hz (~F#4, −1 semitone), alongside Fizeau (1848) & Huggins (1868) spectral-line redshift.

teach_overlay.label: JUNE 1845 UTRECHT TRAIN: G4 HORN (392 HZ) SHIFTS TO ~414 HZ APPROACHING & ~372 HZ RECEDING

teach_overlay.scale: as the locomotive passed the station platform at forty miles an hour, the horn's note plunged by nearly a full piano step in a fraction of a second
